name: forest-band
description: Forest scenery as BAND SEGMENTS rather than strips — 13 midground and 12 foreground pieces, each with open ragged ends so copies butt together into a band as wide as the camera travels. This is what replaces the fixed-width layers in the `forest` pack: place several side by side, repeat as needed, and slide the two bands at different speeds for parallax. Drawn more finely than the flat torn-paper packs, so it reads as a slightly different hand.
stylePrompt:
STYLE — torn and cut paper collage. Every shape is coloured paper cut or torn by hand and laid
flat, with visible deckle edges, paper grain and a dry speckled texture. Seen STRAIGHT ON, flat,
from the front. No vanishing point, no perspective, no lighting, no gradients, no cast shadows.
Palette: muted, warm and mid-century — moss and olive green, deep navy instead of black, brick
red, cream, dusty rose, mustard, soft pink.

The theme is: a forest.

A 5 × 5 sheet of 25 pieces, and these pieces are THE PARTS OF TWO SCENERY BANDS, not separate
objects. They are laid side by side, repeated and overlapped, to build a band as wide as the
stage needs — so each one is a SEGMENT of a band, never a thing standing on its own.
THE RULE THAT MATTERS: every piece must sit next to a copy of itself without a seam showing. So
the LEFT and RIGHT edges are ragged, uneven and open — foliage that carries on, grass that keeps
going — never a straight vertical cut. Each piece is torn out of the middle of a longer band.
The TOP edge is the silhouette against the sky; the BOTTOM edge runs flat and level so pieces
line up on a shared ground line.
13 MIDGROUND pieces: behind the actors, distant, low contrast, a third to half the cell height.
12 FOREGROUND pieces: nearest the audience, darker, larger, more detailed, up to three quarters.
Every piece on a PLAIN WHITE background, no shadow, no ground line drawn under it.
